hints.content:
$(x,y)\to(x+1,y+2)$ tells us how to change the coordinates of $Q$:

- We add $1$ unit to the $x$-coordinate.

- We add $2$ units to the $y$-coordinate.

When we add $1$ unit to the $x$-coordinate, we move the point $1$ unit to the right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with point Q located at negative four, four. The x- and y- axes scale by one. An arrow points from point Q to the right one unit to a spot.

hints.content:
When we add $2$ units to the $y$-coordinate, we move the point $2$ units up.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a point located at negative three, four. The x- and y- axes scale by one. An arrow points up two units from the point to a spot.
